- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- Model shows strong upward bias in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–5 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply downward adjustment for short-term horizon.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with recent mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model, check sentiment history for recent volatility; if sentiment is high, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–5%.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction in next 3–5 days.
